title: Handle a conversion that may fail
summary: TRY_CAST attempts a type conversion. It returns NULL when an ordinary conversion fails, so code can handle the missing result.
introduction: TRY_CAST attempts a type conversion. It returns NULL when an ordinary conversion fails, so code can handle the missing result. Your task: Try converting a different text number.
learningObjectives: Try converting a different text number.
Explain the example for handle a conversion that may fail

blocks.text: TRY_CAST attempts a type conversion. It returns NULL when an ordinary conversion fails, so code can handle the missing result.
Use SQL Server 2019+ in a separate practice database with a SQL editor. T-SQL is different from the SQLite engine on this site, so these examples are for that separate tool.

blocks.code:
SELECT TRY_CAST(N'12' AS int) AS good_value,
       TRY_CAST(N'twelve' AS int) AS missing_value;
blocks.title: Handle a conversion that may fail

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `TRY_CAST` returns NULL for this failed ordinary conversion. Handle that missing value instead of treating it as zero.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: The first value is 12 and the second is NULL.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: NULL is not zero. Check for it before using a failed conversion in important calculations.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Try converting a different text number.
